If there’s one name on people’s lips in Spain this week it’s Maricarmen. The eviction of the 87-year-old from her home, which was later reversed, has sparked a huge wave of spontaneous solidarity in various cities and drawn attention to one of the most pressing problems facing the country: access to housing.

Tens of thousands marched through Madrid on Saturday to protest Maricarmen’s eviction. Some demonstrators camped overnight in Puerta del Sol, where more people, including families of several generations, joined them Sunday, according to the Associated Press. Protesters are demanding stronger tenant protections and a ban on evictions when no other housing is available nearby.

A woman was in custody Saturday after authorities said she stabbed a 7-year-old girl to death near a busy shopping area in the Chatham neighborhood.

The girl, whose identity wasn’t immediately released, was walking south near the 8600 block of South Cottage Grove Avenue when she was approached by an adult woman who was carrying a sharp object around 11:55 a.m., according to Chicago police. In broad daylight, the woman stabbed the girl multiple times in the back, police said.

The girl was rushed to Comer Children’s Hospital, where she was pronounced dead. An autopsy is scheduled for Sunday.

The attacker was injured as bystanders detained her at the scene, police said. She was taken to an area hospital for treatment and placed into police custody, police said.
